heading: 6 Composition and diversity
text:
Ecology offers good tools describing composition landscape.
class_diversity() treats classes species areas abundances
, year, computes richness, Shannon entropy, Pielou evenness, Simpson
indices, Hill numbers dominance:table diversity$change summarises difference first 
last year:first sight, landscape became varied, going 8

entropy stayed flat evenness fell 0.61

area concentrated single dominant class, 
pasture 1985

time:

diversity$plots$indices

heading: 7 Time series
text:
annual maps form 40-year series class. land_time_series()
extracts series interest, soybean (39), pasture (15) forest
formation (3):
code:
series <- land_time_series(areas$time_series, classes = c(39, 15, 3),
                           language = "en")
series$plot

heading: Association between two series
text:
Two trending series often look related even nothing 
one year next. series_correlation() can
measure association levels, annual differences 
residuals trend, corrects p-value autocorrelation:annual differences, correlation soybean pasture 
r = -0.12 (p = 0.46; corrected p =
0.52). words, replacement one class 
clear levels, several years, year--year
changes move together.
code:
correlation <- series_correlation(series, 39, 15, transformation = "difference",
                                  language = "en")
correlation$plots$association

heading: Regimes and change points
text:
series_fit_regime() fits continuous curve transitions regimes.
probabilistic bent-cable model estimates transition happens 
long lasts, bootstrap confidence intervals:soybean story three transitions, 2000
2007: first rapid expansion 
3.6 km² per year, contraction , 
2006 , slow growth. model = "auto", function
compares available models AICc picks suitable one.
code:
fit <- series_fit_regime(series, 39, model = "prob_bent_logistic",
                         bootstrap = 200, seed = 1, language = "en")
fit$plot

heading: Diagnostics and projection
text:
fit explains 98% variation (R²), 
residuals autocorrelated (Durbin-Watson = 1.03;
Ljung-Box, p < 0.001).
residuals depend , intervals tend come narrow. 
case, bootstrap_type = "block" resamples blocks consecutive years 
produces realistic intervals.Finally, series_forecast() extends last regime:projection assumes current regime continues. Read scenario,
prediction future land use change.
code:
diagnostics <- series_diagnostics(fit)
diagnostics$plots$acf
projection <- series_forecast(fit, horizon = 5)
projection$plot

heading: Connectivity at several thresholds
text:

index connectivity (IIC) becomes 9 times
larger. 300 600 m, gain small: species able cross 
300 m, remaining forest already works network.
code:

                                  language = "en")
connectivity$plot

heading: Terrain and roads at Lagoa do Sino
text:
load_physical() brings elevation, slope aspect Copernicus DEM, 
well soil properties SoilGrids (clay, sand, silt, carbon, pH 
others), already resampled map grid. slow connections, worth
raising time limit, defaults 5 seconds:
Figure 11.1: Elevation (Copernicus DEM, 30 m) Lagoa Sino map grid.
load_features() retrieves features Overture Maps regional
OpenStreetMap extracts, feature_raster() turns surfaces 
analysis grid: distance, count, length, coverage density.
Figure 11.2: Distance nearest road (Overture Maps) Lagoa Sino.
field points, distance_to_nearest() measures geodesic distance 
nearest feature land use class. target class maps
, internet connection needed:centre campus 327 m 
nearest forest formation, second point 
847 m away. function also takes 
features load_features(), 
distance_to_nearest(points, roads, feature = "roads").
code:
terrain <- load_physical(maps, layers = c("elevation", "slope"), timeout = 30,
                         language = "en")
terrain$plots$elevation
roads <- load_features(maps, "roads", source = "overture")
distance <- feature_raster(roads, maps, feature = "roads", metrics = "distance",
                           language = "en")
distance$plots$distance
points <- data.frame(lon = c(-48.529, -48.515), lat = c(-23.605, -23.590))
to_forest <- distance_to_nearest(points, maps, classes = 3)
